sources.entry: Harness by revfactory - A meta-skill that designs domain-specific agent teams, defines specialized agents, and generates the skills they use. Resources are in Korean but can produce high-quality English-language output.

summary.one_liner: Harness is a Claude Code plugin/meta-skill that turns a domain description into a team of specialized agents plus the skills and orchestrator they use.
summary.what_it_does: Given a domain description, the harness skill audits any existing harness, analyzes the domain and its control-flow shape, and selects an execution mode and team architecture. It then generates agent definitions under .claude/agents/, skills under .claude/skills/ (including one orchestrator skill that sets the order of work), and a minimal CLAUDE.md pointer. The README describes six architecture patterns (Pipeline, Fan-out/Fan-in, Expert Pool, Producer-Reviewer, Supervisor, Hierarchical Delegation) and three execution modes: Workflow scripts, persistent named agents with SendMessage, and one-shot sub-agent calls. It also covers verification (trigger evals, dry runs, with-skill vs. without-skill A/B tests) and a /harness:evolve skill that turns usage feedback into revisions of agents and skills. Version 2 is described as a rebuild that removes v1's experimental TeamCreate flag dependency and includes a v1 migration path.
use_cases: generate an agent team for a software project
scaffold Claude Code subagents and skills for a domain
design multi-agent workflows with verification loops
migrate a Claude Code multi-agent setup from v1 to v2
evolve agent definitions based on usage feedback
A/B test whether a skill improves agent output
how_to_run: Ask Claude Code: "build a harness for this project" or "하네스 구성해줘"
notable: Chooses execution mode from the shape of the control flow rather than team size, and can mix modes per phase
Includes /harness:evolve, which captures the delta between initial and current harness and feeds feedback back into agents and skills
Built-in detection and mechanical migration for v1 artifacts such as TeamCreate and experimental flags
Per-agent model tier selection (fable / opus / sonnet) instead of blanket pins
Codified quality patterns such as adversarial verification, judge panels, and loop-until-dry
caveats: Prior performance numbers (49.5 to 79.3 mean quality) are author-run on 15 tasks and the README asks users to run their own pilot
Resources and primary interaction are in Korean; the README says English output is achievable but the trigger phrases are Korean-first
The README does not describe support for platforms beyond Claude Code
keywords: set up ai agents for my project
make claude agents for my codebase
